data.raw_text:
Arc isn’t just launching a testnet - it’s quietly positioning itself as the economic operating system of the entire internet. And here’s the part almost no one noticed: for the first time, banks, BigTech, AI companies, and stablecoin issuers have all gathered on the same chain. That doesn’t happen by accident.

Arc isn’t just another L1. Its purpose is to unify traditional money, tokenized assets, global payments, and agentic AI into one standard layer. And not “someday,” but already on testnet.
— National stablecoins from Australia, Brazil, Canada, Japan, Korea, Mexico, and the Philippines aren’t crypto altcoins - they’re a step toward real onchain settlement.
— USDC is used as gas. Predictable fees for enterprises are a core reason this project matters.
— Visa, Mastercard, AWS, Coinbase, Kraken, Uniswap, BlackRock, Deutsche Bank, and dozens of others are already connected - many of whom would never normally coexist in the same environment.
— Under the hood is Malachite, a new BFT engine with sub-second finality. This isn’t a “fast blockchain.” It’s infrastructure designed to plug directly into banking rails.
— And most importantly, Arc is being built to evolve into a collaborative, distributed network - not another corporate-controlled system.

Look at it superficially - it’s just a testnet.
Look deeper - it’s the first attempt to unite the entire financial internet in one layer: payments, liquidity, stablecoins, tokenization, AI agents, and crosschain operations.

For me, Arc is a sign that we’re finally done asking, “When will banks enter crypto?” They’re already here. And now the real question becomes: what kind of internet are we building next - closed, or shared?

@arc

⚠️🚘 TRAFFIC ADVISORY UPDATE (Provincial Government project):

Please be advised of the update received for the ongoing Provincial Government road construction project currently underway on Route 2 - Sherbrooke and Travellers Rest.

🚧Road paving continues this morning (Wednesday, November 26). Once paving is completed, line painting and other finishing touches will occur until the end of the day on Friday (November 28).

👷Once paving is complete, two-way traffic will resume with periodic stop-and-go traffic for large machinery and trucks to move in the area. Please reduce speed and drive with caution around crews working in the area.

❓As this is a Provincial road construction project, and not a project of the City of Summerside, public inquiries into this roadwork should be directed to the Prince Edward Island Department of Transportation and Infrastructure at 902-368-5100.

For more information on this project, please visit the provincial government website at: https://t.co/vPC65h8KLA

#Summerside
